newsitem.title: BELGIUM: CNP sees write back on Elf deal.
newsitem.headline: CNP sees write back on Elf deal.

text.p: Belgian holding company Cie. Nationale a Portefeuille /Nationale Portefeuillemaatschappij (CNP/NPM) said on Thursday it should be able to write back 136 million Belgian francs of provisions in the second half of 1996 following a deal between its controlling shareholder Fibelpar and French oil group Elf.
"Normally we should be able to do this," CNP/NPM chief executive officer Gilles Samyn told Reuters.
CNP/NPM is an investment vehicle of Belgian financier Albert Frere, which in turn controls Swiss based Pargesa Holding and Belgium's Groupe Bruxelles Lambert.
Elf said on Thursday that it sold 7.06 percent, or 1,787,793 shares, of CNP/NPM shares to Fibelpar. Terms were not disclosed.
In a statement, CNP/NPM said the sale effectively cancelled a 1995 agreement between Fibelpar and Elf that allowed Elf to sell it 877,003 CNP/NPM shares at any time up to February 1999.
Under that agreement, CNP/NPM had agreed to compensate Fibelpar for any difference between its share's market price and its net asset value, less 10 percent.
CNP/NPM, which usually trades at more than a 20 percent discount to its net asset value, had booked a 136 million franc provision in its 1995 accounts to cover such a sale.
It was this provision that could now be written back, Samyn said. He said the sale would not alter the control of CNP/NPM, but hoped it could help narrow the discount.
"We are working hard for shareholder value...we're confident that the market will understand us, perhaps not tomorrow, but after certainly," he said.
